findings.title: website_name leaks website data for TL0 users whose website is hidden
findings.body: `website` and `bio_raw`, `location` and similar fields are listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so anonymous viewers of TL0 users do not receive them. `website_name` is not in that list, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?`. For an anonymous viewer of a TL0 user, `website_name` is therefore still serialized, and it now includes the URL path (e.g. `example.com/user`) when the host matches the instance. This bypasses the trust gating the `website` field relies on, and it exposes more of the URL than the host-only value did before. The TL0 spec's untrusted attribute list also does not include `website_name`, so the gap is untested.

findings.title: website_name is parsed and computed repeatedly, and URI errors are swallowed by a modifier rescue
findings.body: `website_name` calls `URI(website.to_s)` up to three times and `website.to_s` each time, and `website` itself goes through `object.user_profile`. The `rescue nil` modifier on the first assignment silently turns any malformed URL into nil with no logging. This is minor, but a single parse with an explicit rescue would be clearer and cheaper.

findings.title: Path appended for a bare-root website yields a trailing slash
findings.body: When the website is `http://example.com/` (path `/`), the same-domain branch returns `example.com/`. A website of `http://example.com` returns `example.com`. The two inputs display differently even though they point to the same site. Normalising the path (or treating `/` as empty) would avoid this.

findings.title: No test that website_name is withheld from anonymous viewers of TL0 users
findings.body: The untrusted attributes list checked by the TL0 context does not include `website_name`, and no test asserts it is hidden when `website` is hidden. Adding `website_name` to that list (and the matching serializer gating) would be covered by such a test, which would have caught the leak.

findings.title: Template now depends on website_name being present, not on the website itself
findings.body: The condition changed from `websiteName` (derived from `model.website`) to `model.website_name`. Because `website_name` is serialized independently of the trust gating on `website`, the link block can render for viewers who see no website URL. The `href` is then empty while the visible text still shows the name. This is coupled to the serializer leak above.

findings.title: Tests stub Discourse.current_hostname but do not cover the 'same length' sibling-subdomain branch
findings.body: The three new tests cover exact match, parent domain, and unrelated domain. The branch where both hosts have the same number of labels and share a registrable domain (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) is not exercised, so a regression in that comparison would go unnoticed.

findings.title: PR description is a placeholder
findings.body: The description reads only 'Test 6' and does not explain the behaviour change (website name now includes the path when the host matches the instance) or the reason for moving display logic from the controller to the serializer. Reviewers have no context for the intended change.
